core_obligations: Reduce to two legs (proof lines 6055-6058): rotating the distinguished triangle, the author assumes that two of the three canonical maps are quasi-isomorphisms.

Choose representatives (proof lines 6056-6061): a map of K-injective complexes is chosen representing the map between the first two complexes, so that the third complex is represented by the cone on that map.

Conclude (proof lines 6062-6066): the canonical map for the third complex is the third leg in a map of distinguished triangles in the homotopy category whose other two legs are quasi-isomorphisms, hence is itself an isomorphism; the closing reference to the general third-isomorphism result covers the remaining compatibility.
proof_roadmap: Rotate the triangle so that the hypothesis concerns the first two terms.
Represent the first two terms by K-injective complexes related by a map, so the third is the cone.
Apply the map of triangles argument to conclude that the third canonical map is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the two out of three statement for the condition that the canonical maps attached to a blow-up square be isomorphisms: if two of the three maps attached to the terms of a distinguished triangle are isomorphisms, so is the third (statement lines 6045-6052). The proof is a complete triangulated argument: after rotating the triangle (proof lines 6055-6058) the author chooses a map of K-injective representatives so that the third complex is the cone (proof lines 6056-6061), and then observes that the canonical map for the third complex is the third leg of a map of distinguished triangles in the homotopy category whose other two legs are quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 6062-6064), invoking the standard third-isomorphism result for the remaining compatibility (proof lines 6065-6066). The non-formal content is the choice of representatives and the map of triangles. The claim is H2: a structured triangulated argument with each input named.
